body: I'd prefer not to introduce a new property for the user. Can we go back to using `cancelled`?
I'm not particularly fond of this shared state, I preferred when it was passed into the function. I think we can fixup this logic.

+          // So, we need to mark it as aborted and stop the routing logic.

body: @Timer currently the `.cancelled` property is being hijacked to also stop the routing logic in cases where the route change isn't explicitly cancelled, like when `getServerSideProps` errors or something. This made those errors being ignored in the routing events. Since an event is already emitted when cancellation happens, all other errors with the `.cancelled` property were ignored. The `.aborted` property was added to distinguish these from real cancellation errors and emit an event for them. I didn't intend for this property to be public, I just needed the `.cancelled` property to be `undefined`. I've changed it to use an internal symbol instead. Not sure if that's an adequate solution?
I made it pass the url to the function again. I also renamed the state to `_inFlightRoute` to make the intent more clear.
